summary: Today's briefing spans a worsening Ebola outbreak and Ukraine's grinding war, a shake-up atop OpenAI and a huge Anthropic acquisition, a landmark physics discovery, and cultural moments from BTS to Deep Purple.

items.title: Ebola outbreak on track to be deadliest ever, WHO chief says
items.description: The WHO warns the current Ebola outbreak has already caused more than 2,000 deaths and is on track to become the deadliest ever recorded.

items.title: Putin can no longer claim victory in Ukraine, Nobel Peace Prize winner tells BBC
items.description: Nobel Peace Prize winner Dmitry Muratov tells the BBC that Putin can only destroy Ukraine, not conquer it, as the war enters its fifth year.

items.title: OpenAI COO Resigns
items.description: OpenAI's chief operating officer has resigned, extending a run of high-profile departures from the company.

items.title: Anthropic in Talks to Buy World Model AI Startup Decart for $6B
items.description: Anthropic is reportedly in talks to acquire world-model startup Decart for around six billion dollars, expanding into generative video and simulation.

items.title: Major Russian grain export terminals hit in Ukraine Black Sea port attack
items.description: Major Russian grain export terminals were struck in a Ukrainian Black Sea attack as both sides hit each other's shipping infrastructure.

items.title: Gemini becomes Google's fastest-growing product ever as it hits 1B users
items.description: Google's Gemini has become the company's fastest-growing product ever, surpassing one billion users.

items.title: As AI safety concerns mount, three pioneers make the case for staying open
items.description: Geoffrey Hinton, Fei-Fei Li and Andrew Ng publicly clashed over AI regulation and open-source access at the Ai4 conference.

items.title: More troops to be sent to West Bank village besieged by Israeli settlers
items.description: More Israeli troops are being sent to a West Bank village where two Palestinian families remain besieged by settlers with water and power cut off.

items.title: At least 44 die as ferry sinks in Zimbabwe's Lake Kariba
items.description: At least 44 people died after a ferry overturned in strong waves on Zimbabwe's Lake Kariba.

items.title: Woman pulled alive from rubble 36 hours after Colombia quake
items.description: A woman was pulled alive from rubble 36 hours after a devastating earthquake struck Colombia.

items.title: Some Claude users are mad that Anthropic’s new watermarks will catch them using it at their jobs, classes
items.description: Some Claude users are angry that Anthropic's new watermarking system could expose their AI use at work or school.

items.title: AI coding startup Cognition reportedly already in talks to raise at $40B valuation
items.description: AI coding startup Cognition is reportedly in talks to raise funding at a forty billion dollar valuation, months after its last round.

items.title: Have physicists finally discovered glueballs? New evidence points to yes.
items.description: Physicists report the strongest evidence yet for glueballs, exotic particles made purely from the strong force's gluons.

items.title: ICE plans to equip agents with gloves that can deliver electric shocks
items.description: US immigration agency ICE is spending twenty million dollars on gloves designed to deliver electric shocks to compel compliance.

items.title: Taiwan says it was hit by ‘abnormal’ AI-assisted cyber-attack
items.description: Taiwan says government agencies were hit by an 'abnormal' AI-assisted cyber-attack, a day after reports of a first-of-its-kind China-linked breach.

items.title: Terabytes of credentials leaked in massive supply-chain attack
items.description: A massive supply-chain attack exfiltrated terabytes of credentials from thousands of users of a compromised AI package.

items.title: Amazon will train on Twitch streamers’ content by default, unless they opt out
items.description: Amazon will train AI on Twitch streamers' content by default, prompting backlash and forcing users to opt out.

items.title: Everything announced at Made by Google ’26: Pixel 11, Pixel Watch 5, Pixel Tag, and tons of Gemini features
items.description: Google's Made by Google 2026 event unveiled the Pixel 11 lineup, a new Pixel Watch and Pixel Tag, alongside a wave of Gemini features.

items.title: JWST images illuminate ‘black hole stars’ at cosmic dawn
items.description: New JWST images illuminate mysterious 'black hole stars' at cosmic dawn, first spotted as tiny red dots in deep-space surveys.

items.title: Stop Killing Games backs Dutch consumer rights lawsuit against Sony's PlayStation digital store "monopoly"
items.description: The Stop Killing Games campaign has joined a Dutch lawsuit accusing Sony of monopolising digital game sales on the PlayStation Store.

items.title: Immortality creator Sam Barlow's new video-scouring game is sci-fi horror Precognition, a collab with filmmaker Brandon Cronenberg, in which you see and change the future
items.description: Immortality creator Sam Barlow has revealed Precognition, a sci-fi horror collaboration with filmmaker Brandon Cronenberg due in 2028.

items.title: Witcher multiplayer spin-off Project Sirius hit by fresh layoffs
items.description: CD Projekt Red has confirmed fresh layoffs on its multiplayer Witcher spin-off Project Sirius amid a broader strategy shift.

items.title: Graduate Student Proves a Quantum Uncertainty Principle for Fractals
items.description: A graduate student has proved a quantum uncertainty principle for fractals, a result hailed as a foundational mathematical breakthrough.

items.title: BTS’ V Reveals Hearing Loss Amid World Tour
items.description: BTS member V revealed during a livestream that he is being treated for hearing loss in his right ear amid the group's world tour.

items.title: Ritchie Blackmore Performs With Deep Purple for First Time Since Acrimonious Split in Early ’90s, After Warning Fans: ‘I Have Not Played Rock Music in 25 Years’
items.description: Guitarist Ritchie Blackmore performed with Deep Purple for the first time since their acrimonious early-1990s split.

items.title: Supermassive Games announces layoffs, up to 75 workers may be affected
items.description: Supermassive Games announced a third round of layoffs in three years, potentially affecting up to 75 staff.

items.title: Meccha Chameleon has now sold 20 million copies in two months
items.description: Indie hide-and-seek game Meccha Chameleon has sold 20 million copies just two months after launch.

items.title: Estrogen-only hormone therapy could lower risk of Alzheimer’s
items.description: A retrospective study finds people on estrogen-only hormone therapy for menopause showed fewer signs of dementia.

items.title: ‘Othello’ Royal Shakespeare Company Adaptation Starring Sharon D. Clarke Postponed as She Undergoes Cancer Treatment
items.description: The Royal Shakespeare Company has postponed its Othello starring Sharon D. Clarke so she can undergo cancer treatment.

items.title: ‘The Wrong Girls’ Review: Kristen Stewart and Alia Shawkat Are a Good Time in Dylan Meyer’s Shaggy Stoner Comedy
items.description: Kristen Stewart and Alia Shawkat headline Dylan Meyer's absurdist stoner comedy The Wrong Girls in a well-received festival debut.
